1.2.840.113549.1.1.name: pkcs-1 (container arc)
1.2.840.113549.1.1.note: Container arc deliberately mapped: every child is RSA-family, so the pseudo-family RSA is never wrong. The padding scheme is NOT derivable here.

1.2.840.113549.1.1.1.name: rsaEncryption
1.2.840.113549.1.1.1.note: PSEUDO-FAMILY. rsaEncryption does not determine the padding scheme, so it cannot yield RSAES-OAEP / RSAES-PKCS1 / RSASSA-PKCS1 / RSASSA-PSS. cbom-lens cdx17map.go makes the same call (bare "RSA" absent from familyExact).

1.2.840.113549.1.1.8.name: id-mgf1
1.2.840.113549.1.1.8.note: CORRECT OID WITH NO LEGAL FAMILY TOKEN. MGF1 is not in algorithmFamiliesEnum. cbomkit emits this asset (keycloak-cbom.json, name 'MGF1', primitive 'other'). Derivation must yield no family rather than an illegal token.

1.2.840.113549.1.1.9.name: id-pSpecified
1.2.840.113549.1.1.9.note: OAEP label parameter; not an algorithm family.

1.2.840.10045.name: ansi-X9-62 (container arc)
1.2.840.10045.note: Homogeneous container: every child is EC-family.

1.2.840.10045.2.1.name: id-ecPublicKey
1.2.840.10045.2.1.note: PSEUDO-FAMILY. Determines EC but not ECDSA-vs-ECDH; primitive / keyUsage decides. Emitted by cbomkit for EC-secp256r1 / EC-secp384r1 / EC-secp521r1.

1.3.132.1.12.name: dhSinglePass-cofactorDH-sha1kdf-scheme
1.3.132.1.12.note: Arc identity INFERRED. Empirically this is the arc three independent producers put on ECDH assets: cbom-lens parse_tls.go (ECDHE-*), cbomkit keycloak-cbom.json (name 'ECDH'), and cyclonedx-bom-examples/CBOM/Protocol/bom.json (name 'X25519' -- itself a mis-stamp; X25519 is 1.3.101.110). Family ECDH is right either way.

1.3.101.110.name: id-X25519
1.3.101.110.note: MODELLING CHOICE: algorithmFamiliesEnum has no X25519 token, so X25519 folds to ECDH + curve other/Curve25519. That fold is ours, not an OID fact.

2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.9.name: id-sha3-384
2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.9.note: THE CORROBORATION TEST CASE. cyclonedx-bom-examples/CBOM/Protocol/bom.json stamps this arc on an asset named 'SHA-384' with parameterSetIdentifier 384. The arc is genuinely id-sha3-384; the producer is wrong. Name must win; conflict must be flagged.

2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.name: aes (container arc)
2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.note: BARE-ARC TOLERANCE, REQUIRED BY REAL DATA. cbomkit emits exactly this arc for 'AES', 'AES128', 'AES128-CBC-PKCS5' and 'AES128-GCM'. Homogeneous subtree, so the family is safe, but neither key size nor mode is derivable -- both stay null.

1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.3.18.name: id-alg-AEADChaCha20Poly1305

nameGrammar.why: cbom-lens ChaCha20-Poly1305 and the unseparated ChaCha20Poly1305 spelling (separator-insensitive: CHACHA20_POLY1305 elected Poly1305 as its family, one construction with two families decided by an underscore)

cbom-lens familyExact, widened twice: the anchored form matched only the bare name, and the two-word HSS-LMS literal that replaced it still let the registered parameter-set names fall through to the SHA-2 rule -- LMS_SHA256_M32_H5 and LMOTS_SHA256_N32_W8 are what RFC 8554 and SP 800-208 register and what a JCA-call scanner emits, so a separator decided whether a stateful hash-based signature was inventoried as a signature or as a digest. Word-guarded on both sides so the bare tokens resolve and nothing matches inside another word; bare HSS is not listed, since the token is also a telecom name
cbom-lens familyExact, widened: XMSS-SHA2_10_256 and XMSS-MT spellings fell through to the SHA-2 rule; the left guard keeps the token from matching inside another word
registry has no Ed25519 family token; EdDSA is the family, Ed25519 the curve
7 corpus rows name the construction rather than its standard; SP800-56C is the registry token for it, and the KDF block runs before the digests so the outer construction wins over the inner hash
cbomkit HMACSHA2 - no separator, so the guarded rule above misses it
MAC tokens must not fall through to their underlying cipher
standalone Poly1305; the size stoplist stops 1305 reading as a size
the registry has no X25519 family token; it is an ECDH variant and the curve carries the rest (11 assets in the wild corpus)
cbomkit ECDH; cbom-lens maps ECDHE- to ECDH; ahead of -RSA
cbom-lens maps DHE- to FFDH; ahead of -RSA
RSA-OAEP and RSAES-OAEP are one algorithm; the short spelling had no rule
RSA-2048-OAEP-SHA256: the size sits between the family and the scheme
RSA-2048-PKCS1v15-SHA256, same interposed-size shape; a digest suffix makes PKCS#1 v1.5 a signature scheme rather than the encryption scheme
RSA-PSS-SHA256: the size-less PSS spelling had no rule and fell to the digest rules, storing an RSA signature asset as a hash. Symmetry with ^RSASSA-PSS
rsa-2048-sha1-signed-key (authoring corpus): the interposed-size form of the existing ^RSA-(?=(SHA|MD)\d) rule — a digest-suffixed RSA name is a signature scheme, never the digest
RSA-PKCS1-1.5-SHA512 (authoring corpus): PKCS#1 v1.5 with a digest is a signature scheme; the cipher-suite classifier had been swallowing it
eclipse-keypont SHA256withRSAandMGF1: MGF1 means PSS, and the old guard blocked on the following 'and' so it read as SHA-2
conformance fixture RSA-SHA256: digest-suffixed RSA is a signature scheme
cbom-lens familyPrefix; MLDSA44 has no separator
cbom-lens familyPrefix; MLKEM768 has no separator

the bare family spelling `SHA2`, as in SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s. Unrecognised it survived into the variant residue as `shas`/`shaf`, which the closed vocabulary then rejected — losing the s/f parameter-set distinction

cbom-lens familyExact RIPEMD-160, widened: the anchored form left a bare `RIPEMD` family-less, and the guard still admits the -160 and -128 spellings. Ranked with the digests rather than in the exact-string block: first rule wins, so from there it outranked HMAC and every signature rule and `HMAC-RIPEMD160`, `RIPEMD160withRSA` and `PBKDF2-HMAC-RIPEMD160` elected the inner hash instead of the outer construction. The rank is part of the rule, so it is stated in the field the artifact carries

3DES before DES. DES3 is in the alternation because the DES rule below admits a trailing digit for DES56 and DES64, so `DES3-CBC` elected DES and keyed identically to `DES-CBC` -- the merge of a broken cipher into a different one
guarded against letters so 'design' cannot match, but DES56 and DES64 are real observed names and a digit must be allowed to follow
cbomkit AES128 / AES128-GCM have no separator; guard blocks RSAES-*
observed spelled out; the bare DH rule cannot match it

registry token with no rule at all until now: `GOST cipher/hash (legacy)` resolved to nothing. One guard, against a following standard number -- 28147, 34.10, 34.11, 34.12 or 34.3, separated by the reference whitespace set or by nothing (`GOST R 34.11-2012`, `GOST_R_34_10_2012`, `GOST28147`, Bouncy Castle's `GOST3411` and `GOSTR3410`) -- because the single registry token cannot carry which standard is meant, so a name citing one stays on the name tier where the number keeps 34.10 apart from 34.11. The guard spells the reference whitespace set rather than an ASCII space: `GOST R 34.10` written with U+00A0 for either space defeated the narrow spelling and merged 34.10 with 34.11 again. Nothing else is guarded: a trailing key size or mode (`GOST-256-CTR`, `GOST-512`) and a glued word (`GOSTHASH`, `GOSTKDF`) elect the family, since a bare `[0-9]` lookahead and a right word guard between them left only six plain-ASCII spellings able to reach it. Cipher suites naming GOST are classified as suites before family derivation runs, so they cannot reach this
registry token with no rule; `Skipjack (broken cipher)` resolved to nothing, and a broken cipher going unnamed is the opposite of what the inventory is for
pseudo-family: a real construction the registry cannot express, 5 corpus rows

pseudo-family: padding scheme unknowable from a bare RSA key
